decisions.reason: As a close-to-core dosimetry instrument that remained prominent on the home page across 2023 and 2024, it fits the firm's established capabilities and appears to have enough traction that the option value of keeping it clearly exceeds its carrying cost.

This oncology risk-management software supports the firm's strategic direction toward integration, automation, and predictive workflows, so with uncertainty still offering upside and software carrying costs relatively manageable, management would likely continue it.

Because this 2024 launch builds on the firm's existing medical imaging QA offer and is still early in its market test, a growing and innovative firm would usually preserve the option while learning more about demand.

Although this mammography phantom is more distant from the core offer and therefore more vulnerable to portfolio pruning, it is still a new 2024 product with limited evidence of failure and likely modest carrying cost, so management would probably keep it for now.

This distant full-field mammography phantom faces the highest risk because it sits farther from the firm's main radiation-therapy-centered base and overlaps with another new mammography item, but the uncertainty is not yet resolved enough to justify an immediate exit.

Medical imaging QA instruments are adjacent to the firm's established strengths and support its broad integrated QA portfolio, so in an expanding firm and growing industry the rational choice is to continue the product while its potential develops.
